startup.name: Replicas
startup.one_liner: Run any coding agent harness in the cloud
startup.description: Replicas is a cloud coding agent that lets engineering teams delegate tickets to Claude Code or Codex from Slack, Linear and an app, each task running in a sandboxed virtual machine with CI feedback loops and preview URLs. Engineering teams would pay per seat or usage. Two founders in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent with a 0.6 to 2 percent band (references/yc_acceptance.md). Up: technical founders in the hottest tooling category, a working product and a concrete workflow. Down: a thin layer over models and harnesses owned by labs, and many similar teams applying. Known to have been accepted, so completeness only.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly decline because cloud coding agents are the most crowded application of the 2025 and 2026 AI wave. Labs, GitHub and Cursor ship the same background agent features, and a reviewer sees little defensibility for a wrapper around Claude Code and Codex with two founders and no stated usage numbers.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely a shutdown or small acqui hire, because model vendors and IDE makers give away the same function and a two person team may not out ship them. Strong paths include a quick pivot toward infrastructure or an acquisition by a developer platform. Even when the company survives, an exit above the cohort median needs revenue growth and a buyer with strategic need, and most acquisitions in the researched set were small and below 100M dollars.

killers.risk: Model labs and IDEs ship the same cloud agents
killers.evidence: Cursor cloud agents, Codex cloud and GitHub Copilot coding agent already run tasks in cloud VMs from Slack and issues.
killers.mitigation: Be harness neutral and own the environment layer.

killers.risk: Thin margin from compute and model costs
killers.evidence: Each task runs a VM plus model tokens, and customers can bring their own subscriptions.
killers.mitigation: Charge for environments and orchestration, not tokens.

killers.risk: Founders lose the race with many parallel entrants
killers.evidence: Many YC companies chase agents orchestration with similar pitches. according to the market research and the analog records cited here
killers.mitigation: Pick a niche such as large monorepos.

killers.evidence: Running a whole codebase and secrets in third party VMs needs reviews.

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating sandboxed VMs, CI feedback loops and multiple harnesses is straightforward for two strong engineers, but reliable environment setup for arbitrary codebases is hard. The software is replicable and the moat must come from environments and workflow.

takeover_risk.rationale: These companies already ship cloud agents and can add Slack and Linear triggers within weeks. They control the models and distribution, so a wrapper has little protection.

narrative.headline: A well timed product in the most crowded corner of AI tooling: a seed is likely, but platform vendors make a lasting Series A hard.
narrative.general_summary: Replicas rides a strong demand wave for coding agents, which makes a seed round likely under the cohort anchor of 55 to 59 percent. The same wave is the reason later steps are hard: Cursor, Codex and GitHub already ship cloud agents with Slack and issue triggers. I hold the Series A near the 26 percent anchor and expect most value to come from a pivot to environments or an acquisition by a developer platform. These numbers are anchored on the 2022 to 2025 cohorts, whose later rounds are not yet fully observed, so the true rates are probably somewhat higher than the known only figures and the uncertainty is wide.
